They don't, but they should. They should get more sets on lifting days. It wasn't intentional. I just usually didn't put it in there because I usually just didn't show it to the athletes, and I would just make them do it.

Usually, for leg days, they would do 3 sets of calves every time they do legs. Sometimes it'll be single-leg resistance, like on a ramp or on a plate or something like deficit calves. Sometimes it'll be bilateral, but they should be treated like any other muscle as well.

Core also needs to get some work, not a lot of work, some work. Some athletes need a lot more rotational core, and that's usually within the programming as well. For field athletes, I have forgotten, but we usually do a couple of core exercises to get them started, and that'll get them started. Usually, about 2 core exercises, then we get into the plyo work, which would be 2 to 3 or 4 different exercises, and then the powerlifting or Olympic lifting, which would be 2 or 3 exercises. Then the 3 to 4 resistance patterns for accessories can take the exercise workouts all the way to 12 to 14 sets.

Rear delts and calves need to get their own sets and reps, yes.
